content.intuition: Since the array is sorted, we can use two pointers starting from both ends. If the sum is too small, move the left pointer right to increase the sum. If the sum is too large, move the right pointer left to decrease the sum.
algorithm_steps: Initialize left pointer at index 0 and right pointer at last index
Calculate sum of elements at both pointers
If sum equals target, return the 1-indexed positions
If sum is less than target, increment left pointer
If sum is greater than target, decrement right pointer

time.explanation: We traverse the array at most once with two pointers moving towards each other

space.explanation: Only using constant extra space for the two pointers

key_insights: Sorted array property enables two-pointer technique
Moving pointers based on sum comparison guarantees finding the solution
No need for extra data structures like hash maps
Each element is visited at most once
common_mistakes: Not handling the case where pointers meet
Using binary search instead of simpler two-pointer approach
Overthinking with hash map when array is already sorted
optimization_notes: This is already the optimal solution for sorted arrays
Cannot improve time complexity below O(n)
Space complexity is already optimal at O(1)
